summary:
AETHERIA-7: ASTRO-HEALTH HUD is a browser-based biomedical telemetry and crew health monitoring dashboard engineered for deep-space missions. Using standard  and real-time digital signal processing, the system performs contactless vital-sign extraction alongside cognitive readiness testing.

Its opto-physiological engine isolates green-channel forehead chrominance (rPPG) from a standard webcam to compute heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV), and optical signal-to-noise ratio, while a dual-sensor fusion engine combines chest optical flow with microphone acoustic envelopes to track respiration rates. The HUD also integrates a NASA-standard Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) to detect cognitive micro-lapses, manual clinical inputs (temperature, SpO2, blood pressure, radiation dosimetry, sleep architecture), and an automated countermeasure engine that calculates an overall Bio-Risk Score and exports telemetry logs in JSON/CSV.

By transforming everyday consumer cameras and microphones into non-invasive, zero-footprint medical sensors, AETHERIA-7 directly addresses the challenge of autonomous crew health monitoring in resource-constrained habitats. Continuous, frictionless tracking of physiological stress, fatigue, and radiation exposure allows astronauts and mission control to detect subtle health anomalies early—preventing mission-critical cognitive errors and ensuring crew safety during long-duration spaceflight.
details:
AETHERIA-7: ASTRO-HEALTH HUD – Live Biomedical Telemetry System

Project Overview

AETHERIA-7 is a browser-based biomedical monitoring dashboard designed around the concept of astronaut health monitoring during space missions. It brings together different physiological measurements and cognitive performance indicators in a single interactive interface. The system aims to demonstrate how an integrated monitoring platform could help track an individual's physical and cognitive condition in demanding environments such as space missions.

How Does It Work?

The system uses a webcam to analyse subtle changes in skin colour, particularly the green colour channel from a selected forehead region, to estimate heart rate through remote photoplethysmography (rPPG). It also analyses chest and shoulder movement to estimate breathing rate. An additional microphone-based method analyses acoustic signals associated with breathing, allowing the system to combine optical and audio information.

The dashboard also includes manual input fields for parameters such as body temperature, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), blood pressure, body mass, radiation exposure readings and sleep stages. A Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) evaluates reaction time and attention by measuring how quickly a user responds to visual stimuli.

These measurements are brought together in a central dashboard that displays live waveforms, physiological readings, performance indicators and an overall bio-risk score. It also provides data export options in JSON and CSV formats for further analysis.

Benefits of the Project

  • Integrates multiple physiological and cognitive monitoring features into one platform.
  • Demonstrates non-contact methods of estimating heart rate and breathing rate using commonly available devices.
  • Provides a visual representation of physiological signals and measurements.
  • Includes cognitive performance testing to assess alertness and reaction time.
  • Allows data to be exported for record-keeping and further analysis.
  • Explores affordable and accessible approaches to health-monitoring technology.

Intended Impact

The main objective is to explore how technology can support continuous astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions. Astronauts may experience changes in their physiological condition, sleep patterns and cognitive performance due to isolation, altered sleep cycles and the spaceflight environment.

AETHERIA-7 demonstrates the concept of combining different monitoring methods into one platform. The broader aim is to encourage the development of accessible, integrated monitoring systems that could support future space-health research and mission planning.

Tools, Programming Languages and Technologies Used

  • HTML5: Developed the structure and layout of the dashboard.
  • CSS3 and Tailwind CSS: Designed the interface, styling and responsive layout.
  • JavaScript: Implemented sensor processing, signal analysis, calculations, interactive features and data handling.
  • Webcam and browser camera APIs: Captured video for optical heart-rate and chest-motion analysis.
  • Web Audio API: Captured and analysed audio signals for respiration monitoring.
  • HTML Canvas: Displayed real-time physiological waveforms and visual indicators.
  • JSON and CSV: Enabled the export of collected and entered data.

The project is designed to run through a web browser and uses its built-in camera and microphone capabilities. It also provides manual input options for measurements that require external instruments.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of AETHERIA-7 lies in bringing together different monitoring approaches in a single space-themed biomedical dashboard. Instead of focusing on only one physiological parameter, it combines optical heart-rate estimation, respiration monitoring, manual health measurements, sleep information and cognitive performance testing.

Another innovative aspect is its use of readily available devices, such as a webcam and microphone, to demonstrate contactless physiological monitoring techniques. The futuristic telemetry interface presents complex measurements in a format inspired by spacecraft monitoring systems.

Design Considerations

During the development of the project, several factors were considered:

  • Accessibility: Using commonly available computer hardware, such as webcams and microphones.
  • Multiple monitoring methods: Providing alternative approaches when camera or microphone access is unavailable.
  • Signal quality: Considering background noise, lighting conditions, movement and other factors that can affect measurements.
  • User interaction: Creating a clear dashboard that presents different parameters in an organised and understandable way.
  • Data management: Including options to export readings for future reference and analysis.
  • Space-mission relevance: Designing the system around the physiological and cognitive monitoring challenges associated with long-duration spaceflight.
  • Privacy: Requiring browser permission before accessing the camera and microphone.

Conclusion

AETHERIA-7 demonstrates how web technologies, signal processing and biomedical monitoring concepts can be combined to explore astronaut health monitoring. By integrating physiological measurements, respiration analysis and cognitive performance testing into one platform, the project presents a conceptual approach to supporting human health and performance during future space missions.
